about.title: Colton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Colton recorded 14 traffic deaths alongside 452 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, numbers that represent families across San Bernardino County left to navigate grief and unanswered questions. Many of these losses trace back to Colton's busiest corridors, including I-215, I-10, and Mt Vernon Avenue, where reported crashes cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. When a crash claims a family member, California law allows certain surviving relatives to pursue a wrongful death claim separate from any criminal proceedings tied to the crash. LawProactive is not a law firm, but we connect grieving families in Colton with independent personal injury attorneys who handle these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. You don't need to sort through legal deadlines or paperwork alone while carrying this kind of loss.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Colton Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, typically starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help your family understand where you stand before time runs short.

items.title: The Filing Window Is Only Two Years
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter deadline. Acting sooner preserves evidence and protects your family's legal options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs and lost financial support, as well as the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the person provided. An attorney can help make sure none of these losses are overlooked.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and clarify who may bring the claim.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after a fatal crash in Colton?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, such as those maintained near I-215 or I-10 in San Bernardino County, the deadline can be much shorter. Speaking with an attorney early helps avoid missing this window.

items.question: Will pursuing a wrongful death claim interfere with any criminal case?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may result from the crash. The two proceedings can move forward independently of one another. An attorney can explain how each process may affect your family's situation.
